statements.status_notes: The affected name-constraints deinitialization code was introduced in GnuTLS 3.8.13 (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/22cba2f35742cef9137de8f1bcbde6ef15e2e979). This package is built from GnuTLS 3.8.9 sources, which do not contain that code, so the defect is not present. Upstream fix: https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/95256a91bbf1e5f15f75bbd0454c7b05f7b4858a. Advisory: GNUTLS-SA-2026-11-18-3.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS fix (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/8767518753a633e5ef59f112310db8dc9ff6771a): the RSA-PSK client key exchange returns the error when copying the PSK username fails. Advisory: GNUTLS-SA-2026-11-18-2.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS fix (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/0cf60141ca2c1289e96847261ff355010cb6f3a8): the certificate list is always zeroized after it is cleaned up. Advisory: GNUTLS-SA-2026-11-18-1.

DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is under investigation for this CVE. The CVE describes a critical keyUsage extension that is not rejected when it cannot be processed. No candidate fix was identified in the name-constraint and SAN backport set evaluated for this change, so nothing is backported or verified here. The upstream CVE record does not treat this as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, which this package does not adopt. Revisit when a fix is identified, backported, and tested against this package.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed, and a directoryName constraint rejects any leaf with a non-empty subject DN because DN matching is not implemented. A CA whose permitted directoryName constraint is O=Good rejects a leaf with subject O=Evil, with only the root trusted; the same chain under an unconstrained intermediate is accepted. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

Fixed in this package by backporting the upstream GnuTLS name-constraint corrections (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/6e11fea0d5c5886bd215b81fb35baf10b031c8d8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/261c718f998351e71db3590a8df78b15961e7e26, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/988f435abdd33c66c75ca2069118e9f1c7fb0206, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/5d1d734f596d89842c7134d5b43c25f45f0306ec), adapted to GnuTLS 3.8.9. Unsupported name constraint types fail closed. A CA constraint on an SRVName (otherName OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.8.7) rejects a leaf that carries an SRVName, and an excluded SRVName constraint rejects the chain even when the leaf carries no SRVName. The same SRVName under an unconstrained CA is accepted. UPN, URI and directoryName constraints are covered by the same tests. Verified by runtime tests on the amd64 and arm64 candidates.

DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is under investigation for this CVE. The name-constraint backport for the unsupported-constraint paths (upstream 6e11fea0, 261c718f, 988f435a, 5d1d734f) is present in this build, but no runtime test covers this CVE's path, so it is not claimed as fixed. The upstream CVE record does not treat this as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, which this package does not adopt. Revisit when the path is identified and tested.

DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is under investigation for this CVE. The upstream CVE record says the supplier does not treat it as actionable under its trust-boundary threat model, but this package does not adopt that as a justification. No candidate fix for the KU/EKU contradiction was found in the name-constraint and SAN backport set evaluated for this change, so nothing is backported or verified here. Revisit when a fix is identified, backported, and tested against this package.

DHI gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4+dhi3 is built with --disable-tls11-support (upstream 4ff381e6, RFC 8996), which disables TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and DTLS 1.0 at configure time. In the built package the protocol list contains only VERS-TLS1.2, VERS-TLS1.3 and VERS-DTLS1.2, and TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 priorities are rejected; a TLS 1.2 handshake and a TLS 1.3 handshake succeed. Verified by package/deb/main/gnutls28/tests (TestLegacyTLSVersionsAreDisabled).
